paper_title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. Although Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) can jointly generate text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely underexplored. Progress in this area is hindered by two key limitations: (1) the lack of well-defined interleaved generation tasks and corresponding training data, and (2) the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can reliably diagnose model performance across different capability dimensions. To this end, we present IntReal, comprising two complementary components: IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of multimodal interleaved samples spanning four major categories, and the IntReal Evaluation Suite, which evaluates model performance across seven complementary dimensions using specialized expert models, enabling coarse-to-fine diagnosis. Extensive experiments validate our evaluation suite through low inter-metric redundancy (max pairwise absolute Spearman's $ρ\leq 0.42$ ), high agreement with human judgments (83.3% accuracy), and strong consistency across different expert evaluators (Spearman's $ρ> 0.9$ ), supporting the complementarity and reliability of our metrics. By benchmarking four families of UMMs, we show that IntReal Evaluation Suite reveals distinct strengths and weaknesses across models. Post-training experiments demonstrate the utility of IntReal-100K for improving interleaved generation and further show that training unimodal generation can also benefit interleaved generation. These findings suggest that interleaved generation can benefit from modality-specific optimization, rather than requiring joint text-image training at every stage.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Flip through book or browse webpage, and text and images are often tightly interleaved. Encyclopedic articles interleave text and images to communicate knowledge, storybooks integrate narratives with vivid illustrations, tutorials pair step-by-step instructions with corresponding visual demonstrations, and travel guides present itineraries alongside maps and photographs. Despite the emergence of Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) capable of generating both text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely treated as by-product of model unification rather than fundamental generative task in its own right (Deng et al., 2025; Cui et al., 2025; Diao et al., 2026). major reason for this underexploration is the lack of datasets and benchmarks specifically designed for this task. On the data side, as shown in table 1, large-scale interleaved datasets such as MMC4 (Zhu et al., 2023), OBELICS (Laurencon et al., 2023) and OmniCorpus (Li et al., 2025b) are primarily collected for multimodal understanding rather than generation, and therefore do not provide generation-oriented quality control. CoMM (Chen et al., 2025c) aggregates interleaved data sources, but does not organize data collection around taxonomy of real-world scenarios, leaving the task space of multimodal interleaved generation insufficiently characterized. This field thus lacks high-quality interleaved generation dataset constructed under principled taxonomy. On the evaluation side, as shown in table 2, existing benchmarks often rely on vision-language models (VLMs) to holistically assess long interleaved responses (Zhou et al., 2025b; Liu et al., 2024), which is inherently misaligned with the fine-grained evaluation required to characterize complex generative capabilities (Huang et al., 2024). Recent studies improve evaluation granularity through modalityspecific decomposition or structured verification (Li et al., 2026b). For example, ISG-Bench (Chen et al., 2025a) decomposes responses into four levels of structural granularity, but this decomposition does not map onto distinct capability dimensions. Moreover, it relies solely on VLM evaluator across all levels, which may lack the specialized competence some dimensions require. To address these limitations, we introduce IntReal, real-world dataset and benchmark tailored to multimodal interleaved generation. We first identify four core generation scenarios from real-world interleaved content and organize them into taxonomy. Guided by this taxonomy, we apply both understanding-oriented and generation-oriented filtering to million-scale pool of raw interleaved data, resulting in IntReal-100K, high-quality real-world dataset containing 538K images. Building on IntReal-100K, we further develop the IntReal Evaluation Suite, an evaluation framework grounded in real-world scenarios. Specifically, we construct an evaluation set through stringent automated filtering and expert curation. We then evaluate interleaved generation in two complementary settings: (1) holistic generation of complete interleaved responses to assess open-ended capabilities and (2) next-image generation conditioned on interleaved contexts for controlled diagnosis. Across both settings, we integrate specialized expert evaluators, such as image quality assessment (IQA) models, into seven metrics, enabling fine-grained diagnosis from diverse perspectives. We conduct extensive experiments to assess IntReal Evaluation Suite and the utility of IntReal100K for training UMMs. First, we examine three properties of the suite. Its seven metrics show low redundancy (maximum pairwise absolute Spearman correlation below 0.42), suggesting that they capture distinct capability dimensions. Automatic evaluations agree with human judgments in 83.3% of cases, while results remain consistent across different expert evaluators (Spearman correla-

Second, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on IntReal-100K improves text generation in models such as SenseNova-U1 (Diao et al., 2026), but degrades aspects of image generation, echoing the well-known tension between optimizing text and image generation in UMMs. Given the limited exploration of reinforcement learning for interleaved generation, we apply Flow-GRPO (Liu et al., 2025) to next-image generation conditioned on interleaved contexts, while testing whether our metrics can serve as effective reward signals. Flow-GRPO recovers the degraded image generation capability and achieves the highest overall score among the open-source UMMs we evaluate on IntReal Evaluation Suite. These results show that training single generation modality can improve interleaved generation, opening up optimization paths beyond conventional SFT on multimodal interleaved data. Together, these experiments show that IntReal-100K supports effective training of UMMs for interleaved generation, while IntReal Evaluation Suite accurately and reliably identifies strengths and weaknesses across multiple capability dimensions. Overall, our main contributions are summarized as follows: 1. Real-world dataset. We introduce IntReal-100K, taxonomy-guided dataset for multimodal interleaved generation containing 100K high-quality, real-world interleaved sequences. Experiments demonstrate its utility for improving the interleaved generation capabilities of UMMs. 2. Fine-grained data-driven benchmark. We develop IntReal Evaluation Suite, data-driven benchmark that assesses interleaved generation across seven capability dimensions through coarse-to-fine evaluation. Three validation studies show that its metrics have low redundancy, align well with human judgments, and remain consistent across different expert evaluators. 3. Modality-specific gains transfer to interleaved generation. We show that optimizing image generation under interleaved contexts can improve overall multimodal interleaved generation capability. This finding expands the optimization space beyond joint SFT on interleaved sequences.

sections.title: 2 REAL-WORLD INTERLEAVED DATASET CONSTRUCTION
sections.content: 2.1 CHARACTERIZING REAL-WORLD INTERLEAVED CONTENT Web pages and videos are among the most abundant sources of naturally interleaved multimodal content. We collect million-scale raw corpus of interleaved text-image content from seven sources that permit public collection and redistribution. Based on the functional roles and collaboration patterns between text and image, we analyze the collected data and identify four categories: Planning: Decision making under user-specific goals and constraints. Text provides detailed information under given objectives, preferences, and constraints, while images visualize the corresponding spatio-temporal changes. We collect content from WikiVoyage and WikiTravel. Knowledge: Explaining concepts through real-world knowledge. Text conveys concepts and explanations, while images provide corresponding visual representations and help ground abstract knowledge. We collect such encyclopedia content from Wikipedia. Tutorial: Executing tasks through temporally ordered instructions. Text describes procedural steps, while images illustrate intermediate states and temporal transitions to align instructions with execution, such as cooking tutorials. This category includes data collected from Xiachufang. Story: Expressing ideas through narrative-driven content creation. Text drives narrative progression, while images construct characters and scenes. Inspired by SEED-Story (Yang et al., 2025b), this category includes data collected from The Land Before Time, Rabbids, and Curious George. As illustrated in fig. 1, we visualize representative examples from the four representative categories identified above. Licensing details for each source are discussed in Appendix A.1. 2.2 DATA COLLECTION AND CURATION High-quality training data for interleaved generation requires both individual modality quality and strong cross-modal alignment. To this end, we design multi-stage curation pipeline that progressively improves data quality from low-cost filtering to high-cost semantic polishing, producing interleaved data for training UMMs. Specifically, we first apply low-cost visual quality filters to

sections.content: Figure 2: Overview of the IntReal Evaluation Suite. We select 600 high-quality samples from IntReal-100K to construct this suite. Each sample is evaluated at two granularities: holistic evaluation generates the complete interleaved sequence at once, while fine-grained evaluation generates the next image conditioned on the preceding interleaved context to enable controllable diagnosis. remove noisy and low-quality samples. We then leverage VLMs to polish textual descriptions while preserving their original factual content, improving readability and cross-modal consistency. The overall pipeline consists of the following stages (see Appendix A.2 for detailed filtering criteria): Step 1: Metadata-based Filtering. We first filter images by file metadata, removing those with abnormal aspect ratios, low resolution, or unsupported formats to ensure basic visual quality. Step 2: Representation-based Filtering. We employ representation-based specialized visual models to identify and remove undesirable content. Specifically, we use the RALI (Zhao et al., 2026) Image Quality Assessment (IQA) model to filter low-quality images, and finetune SigLIP2 (Tschannen et al., 2025) classifiers on expert-annotated in-domain data to detect watermarks and human faces. We further perform intra-sequence deduplication using DINOv3 (Simeoni et al., 2025) to remove near-duplicate images, ensuring both visual quality and diversity within each sample. Step 3: VLM-based Refinement. We employ Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (Qwen Team, 2026a) to generate image captions and polish the surrounding text, following principle that prioritizes original text over generated captions to preserve factual authenticity while improving text-image consistency. Step 4: LLM-based Annotation. We use Qwen3.5-397B-A17B to generate prompts and reasoning processes conditioned on the original content and its category, transforming each sample into structured multimodal interleaved data that can be directly used to fine-tune UMMs. After the above curation process, we perform category-balanced sampling to ensure basic balance across four categories. Only about 10% of the collected samples are ultimately retained, as any defective segment within long interleaved sample leads to its removal. This process results in high-quality interleaved dataset, IntReal-100K, with category statistics provided in Appendix A.3.

sections.title: 3 REAL-WORLD DATA-DRIVEN EVALUATION
sections.content: As shown in fig. 2, we build our evaluation suite on real-world interleaved samples from IntReal100K, combining coarse-to-fine protocol with expert-guided, multi-dimensional assessment.

sections.title: 3.1 EVALUATION SET CONSTRUCTION
sections.content: To construct reliable evaluation set, we adopt semi-automatic curation strategy to select highquality samples from IntReal-100K (see Appendix B.1 for details). Specifically, we first build an automatic candidate pool by evaluating three key dimensions of interleaved sample quality: Text Quality: We leverage Qwen3.5-397B-A17B to assess textual quality from three perspectives: prompt specificity, response richness, and topic informativeness. Image Quality: We use RALI to retain samples with high-quality images. Text-Image Alignment: We adopt context-aware self-verification strategy using Qwen3.5397B-A17B. For each image, the model first derives visual rubrics specifying what the image should depict from the preceding text-image context, without accessing the target image. It then checks the target image against rubrics to filter out samples with cross-modal inconsistencies. We adjust the filtering thresholds to obtain high-quality candidate pool of manageable size, then manually remove samples that fail to meet the quality criteria. Finally, we perform stratified sampling by category to construct balanced evaluation set of 600 samples, with 150 per category. We opt for relatively compact evaluation set, since our coarse-to-fine protocol already requires generating over 6,000 images interleaved with text per model. Scaling further would substantially increase evaluation cost across multiple model families without commensurate benefit. 3.2 EXPERT MODEL-BASED COARSE-TO-FINE BENCHMARKING To evaluate UMMs in coarse-to-fine manner, we design two complementary settings for interleaved generation. Holistic evaluation assesses complete interleaved responses generated from scratch. Fine-grained evaluation tests next-image generation under fixed real-world interleaved contexts. These shared contexts enable controlled, fine-grained comparisons across models. The two settings are illustrated in fig. 2. We design seven metrics to assess distinct capabilities of interleaved generation, where and denote metrics used for holistic and fine-grained evaluation, respectively: Text Richness (H): We employ an LLM as text modality expert to compare generated textual responses with corresponding real-world textual responses through pairwise ranking, evaluating the richness and informativeness of generated texts. Text Logicality (H): Using the same LLM-based text expert, we assess whether generated texts contain factual errors, contradictions, or logical inconsistencies. Image Aesthetic (H): We employ an IQA model as visual modality expert to measure the average aesthetic quality of generated images. Image Diversity (H): We identify visual repetition as common failure mode, where images generated at consecutive positions may become overly similar and fail to reflect the progression of the context. To quantify this issue, we compute the DINO feature similarity between adjacent generated images, where extremely high similarity indicates potential visual repetition. Quantity Compliance (H): We use the number of images in the corresponding real-world sample as the target quantity and require the model to generate the same number, thereby evaluating instruction following with an image budget known to be sufficient for conveying the content. Context Fidelity (F): We assess whether generated next images are consistent with their preceding interleaved context. We employ VLM as multimodal expert to verify whether each generated image satisfies the visual rubrics constructed during evaluation set curation in section 3.1. Subject Consistency (F): We compute DINO similarity between generated image and their corresponding reference image at the same positions in interleaved samples to measure whether key visual subjects remain consistent, e.g., story characters or cooking ingredients. Detailed formulations of metrics are provided in Appendix B.2. All metrics are evaluated across all categories, except Subject Consistency, which is computed only for Tutorial and Story. This is because Knowledge and Planning do not necessarily require consistent subjects across images.

sections.title: 4 EXPERIMENT
sections.content: 4.1 EXPERIMENTAL SETUP We evaluate four families of UMMs with varying levels of support for interleaved generation and fine-tuning: (1) Bagel (Deng et al., 2025), which provides official fine-tuning scripts but whose released checkpoint does not natively support interleaved generation. We therefore report only its performance after fine-tuning on IntReal-100K. (2) Emu3.5 (Cui et al., 2025), which supports native interleaved inference but does not release fine-tuning methods. We thus evaluate only its original checkpoint. (3) SenseNova-U1 (Diao et al., 2026), which supports both fine-tuning and interleaved inference, allowing evaluation before and after fine-tuning on IntReal-100K. SenseNova-U1 provides two variants, 8B-MoT and A3B-MoT. Both use an 8B generation branch, while their understanding components adopt an 8B and 30B-A3B MoE architecture, respectively. For 8B-MoT, the authors additionally release SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Interleaved, checkpoint specifically optimized for this task. To ensure strong baseline, we adopt this checkpoint for our evaluation and finetuning. No corresponding specialized checkpoint is released for A3B-MoT, for which we therefore evaluate the standard model. Due to computational constraints, we report fine-tuned results only for the 8B-MoT variant. (4) NanoBanana2 (Gemini3.1-Flash-Image), which is closed-source API supporting interleaved generation. Since the system is not publicly disclosed, we cannot determine whether this capability is native or implemented through an agentic pipeline. Other models are excluded if they are unavailable or lack publicly released implementations required for our finetuning and evaluation such as LLaDA2.0-Uni (AI et al., 2026). In addition, Anole (Chern et al., 2024) and Show-o2 (Xie et al., 2025b) are excluded from our evaluation because their released models are limited in context length and cannot support the long-context interleaved generation setting. For evaluation, we use Gemma4 (Team et al., 2026a) for both LLMand VLM-based judging due to its strong performance, open-source availability, and modest computational requirements. For fine-tuning, we use the official training framework of each model for SFT, while all RL experiments are implemented with Flow-Factory (Ping et al., 2026). All post-training data are drawn from the 99.4K samples in IntReal-100K after excluding the 600 samples used in the IntReal Evaluation Suite, ensuring that the training and evaluation sets are strictly disjoint. Additional evaluation details are provided in Appendix B, and further training and inference details are provided in Appendix C. 4.2 BENCHMARKING UMMS ON INTREAL Table 3 presents the per-dimension IntReal evaluation results, while fig. 3 further reports the results across different categories. From these results, we make the following observations.

sections.content: Figure 3: IntReal evaluation results per category. We report the score of each metric for each category, computed by averaging over UMMs. Figure 4: Spearman correlations across metrics with different VLM evaluators. The consistent model rankings demonstrate the robustness of our evaluation method. Different UMMs exhibit distinct and complementary capabilities. No single model performs consistently well across all evaluation dimensions. Among open-source models, Emu3.5 achieves the strongest Text Logicality, while U1-8B-MoT performs substantially better in Quantity Compliance and Context Fidelity. The closed-source NanoBanana2 also does not uniformly outperform open-source models, showing advantages on unimodal dimensions such as Text Richness, Text Logicality, and Image Aesthetic, while remaining below the best open-source results on interleavedspecific dimensions such as Image Diversity and Context Fidelity. These results suggest that strong unimodal capabilities are important for interleaved generation, but are not sufficient on their own, as interleaved generation also requires optimization for interleaved-specific dimensions. Different categories emphasize distinct capabilities. Planning and Knowledge are more demanding in Text Richness and Text Logicality, while Tutorial is particularly challenging under finegrained evaluation, with lower Context Fidelity and Subject Consistency. Story often requires longer interleaved sequences, leading to greater challenges in Quantity Compliance and Image Diversity. OSS UMMs exhibit imbalanced multimodal capabilities. The largest gap between open-source UMMs and the closed-source API lies in the text modality, whereas the gap in image modality is substantially smaller. This asymmetry is consistent with recent findings on scaling UMMs (Tong et al., 2026; Wang et al., 2026), where language is more parameter-hungry while vision is more datahungry. Given that current OSS UMMs remain much smaller than todays flagship LLMs, scaling model capacity may be one of the most important steps toward stronger interleaved generation. 4.3 POST-TRAINING ON INTREAL-100K Compared with the original U1-8B-MoT, SFT improves Text Richness, Text Logicality, and Subject Consistency by 29.04%, 6.68%, and 6.53%. However, Image Aesthetic and Context Fidelity decrease by 5.65% and 4.89%, revealing trade-off between different capabilities. This degradation may arise from the inherent optimization conflict between understanding and generation in UMMs. We therefore investigate whether Reinforcement Learning (RL) can alleviate this trade-off. To close the loop, we validate whether the metrics introduced in section 3.2 can serve as effective learning signals. We first select 10K high-quality RL samples and annotate them with rubrics following the same procedure in section 3.1. We then apply FlowGRPO (Liu et al., 2025) using IQA, DINO, and rubric-based rewards for optimization. For U1-8B-MoT, RL substantially mitigates the degradation in Image Aesthetic and Context Fidelity introduced by SFT, while further improving Image Diversity. similar trend holds for Bagel before and after RL in Image Aesthetic and Context Fidelity, while its already-high Image Diversity remains stable. Overall, U1-8B-MoT with SFT and RL achieves the highest mean score among all OSS models, indicating that improvements in image-generation capability can effectively transfer to interleaved generation. case study of U18B-MoT under different post-training settings is shown in fig. 7.

sections.title: 5 RELATED WORK
sections.content: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs). Existing research on UMMs has primarily explored two complementary directions. The first seeks to unify text and image generation within single model (Ramesh et al., 2021; Sun et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2025a; Zhou et al., 2025a; Chen et al., 2025b; Zhang et al., 2026; Yang et al., 2025a; Dong et al., 2024; Team et al., 2026b; Li et al., 2026c). Representative studies combine multimodal understanding with text-to-image generation, while subsequent works further incorporate image editing and other any-to-image tasks to enable image generation conditioned on multimodal contexts (Xie et al., 2025a; Wu et al., 2025b; Liu et al., 2026b; Team, 2025). The second treats interleaved text-image sequences as native form of multimodal pretraining rather than collection of separate downstream tasks (Cui et al., 2025; Tong et al., 2026; Han et al., 2026; Tian et al., 2024; Kou et al., 2024; AI et al., 2026). Multimodal Interleaved Datasets and Benchmarks. Early interleaved datasets were primarily developed for multimodal understanding and pretraining, constructed through text-based synthesis or web-scale collection (Zhu et al., 2023; Laurencon et al., 2023; Li et al., 2025b; Awadalla et al., 2024). CoMM (Chen et al., 2025c) further introduces generation-oriented filtering, making interleaved data more suitable for generation tasks. Recent studies have shifted toward enabling models to learn multimodal reasoning traces (Gu et al., 2026; Li et al., 2026a). On the evaluation side, early benchmarks mainly define diverse downstream tasks for interleaved generation and commonly rely on VLMs for holistic assessment (Zhou et al., 2025b; Liu et al., 2024). UEval (Li et al., 2026b) and ISG-Bench (Chen et al., 2025a) take steps toward fine-grained evaluation by decoupling interleaved responses into more structured evaluation targets. Meanwhile, Uni-MMMU (Zou et al., 2026) and RealUnify (Shi et al., 2026) benchmark the bidirectional synergy between understanding and genIn contrast, eration through tasks that explicitly couple textual reasoning and visual generation. WEAVE (Chow et al., 2026) evaluates UMMs over multi-turn interleaved text-image contexts, with each turn producing single-modality response. Beyond UMMs, UniM (Li et al., 2026d) evaluates omni-modal models under arbitrary combinations of inputs and outputs across multiple modalities.

sections.title: 6 CONCLUSION
sections.content: In this work, we systematically study multimodal interleaved generation from the perspectives of application scenarios, data construction, evaluation, and post-training. We first characterize four representative real-world scenarios and develop taxonomy-guided data curation pipeline to construct IntReal-100K from real-world content. Building upon these data, we introduce the IntReal Evaluation Suite, which follows coarse-to-fine evaluation principle and integrates specialized expert models to provide complementary measurements across seven dimensions. Our experiments reveal that SFT on IntReal-100K brings gains but also introduces trade-offs across different capabilities. Through Flow-GRPO, we further show that the proposed metrics can serve as effective learning signals, and that improving unimodal generation capability can generalize to multimodal interleaved generation. These findings suggest that modality-specific optimization can improve interleaved generation, expanding the training options beyond joint optimization of text and image generation. IntReal also has several limitations. Constructing high-quality real-world interleaved data requires aggressive filtering and thus yields relatively low retention rate. In addition, we do not explore mixed post-training with unimodal generation data to maintain clean experimental setting. We leave synthetic data augmentation and mixed-data post-training for future work.

sections.content: A.1 DATA SOURCES AND LICENSING Wikivoyage. Wikivoyage is collaborative, community-edited travel guide hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation. It provides destination-oriented articles covering attractions, transportation, accommodation, local customs, and suggested itineraries, making it natural source of planningoriented interleaved content. Textual content on Wikivoyage is released under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike license, which permits copying, redistribution, and adaptation provided that appropriate attribution is given and derivative works are distributed under the same or compatible license. Images and other media may be subject to file-specific licenses, and we retain the corresponding provenance and licensing information when collecting the data. Our use and release of Wikivoyage-derived content follow the applicable attribution and share-alike requirements. Wikitravel. Wikitravel is collaboratively written travel guide containing destination descriptions, and itinerary-oriented content contributed by its community. Its structured combination of descriptive text and travel-related images provides another source of planning-oriented multimodal sequences in IntReal. All Wikitravel-derived data released in IntReal follow these licensing conditions. Wikipedia. Wikipedia is collaboratively maintained online encyclopedia hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation, covering broad range of real-world concepts, entities, events, and scientific topics. This process improves text-image consistency and converts the collected content into trainable supervision while preserving its factual authenticity. Filtering Rules. For metadata-based filtering, we retain images with aspect ratios between 1:2 and 2:1 and exclude unsupported formats, including GIF and WebP. We further impose source-specific minimum resolution requirements on the shorter side of each image. Specifically, we require minimum shorter-side resolution of 512 pixels for Wikivoyage, Wikitravel, Wikipedia, and Xiachufang, while using threshold of 384 pixels for the three story sources. The relaxed threshold for story data accounts for the relatively low native resolution of older animated content, whose shorter side frequently falls below 512 pixels. For representation-based filtering, we adapt the activation of different filters according to the characteristics of each source. Since Xiachufang primarily consists of user-uploaded content, we apply both face and watermark filtering to remove potentially undesirable user-generated images. We fine-tune one SigLIP2-based (Tschannen et al., 2025) binary classifier for these tasks using 5000 manually annotated Xiachufang samples, achieving an F1 score of 0.82 on the held-out test set. In contrast, we do not apply face filtering to the three Wiki-based sources, since human faces often constitute semantically necessary content, such as portraits of notable individuals, while these sources already undergo platform-level content moderation and rarely contain intrusive watermarks. Similarly, face filtering is not applied to the three story sources, where recurring characters constitute essential visual subjects and should be preserved. Across all sources, we additionally apply RALI-based (Zhao et al., 2026) image quality filtering and DINO-based intra-sequence deduplication. For RALI, we require each individual image to obtain score above 3.0 and the average score of all images within sample to exceed 3.5. For DINO-based deduplication, adjacent images are required to have feature similarity below 0.85, which removes highly repetitive visual sequences while preserving meaningful visual continuity. Content Refinement and Annotation. After filtering, all retained samples undergo four-stage refinement and annotation pipeline to improve text-image alignment while preserving the factual content of the original sources. First, we generate detailed captions for each image to recover visual information that may be absent from the surrounding text. Second, we refine the original textual content by incorporating complementary information from the generated captions, while explicitly preserving the facts and semantics of the source content. Third, we construct hierarchical annotations at both the sequence and image levels: for each interleaved sample, we annotate its user prompt and generate sequence-level reasoning trace, while each individual image is additionally associated with an image-specific reasoning trace describing its role and generation rationale within the sequence. Finally, we jointly refine the complete prompt and interleaved content to further improve their global consistency and coherence. Through this process, the collected web content is transformed into training-ready interleaved data with improved multimodal alignment, structured supervision, and preserved factual fidelity. A.3 DATASET STATISTICS Table 4 presents the statistics of IntReal-100K across different categories and data sources. Different categories exhibit distinct structural characteristics. Planning data are relatively concise, with fewer images and shorter text per sample, while Knowledge and Tutorial data contain richer multimodal content. Xiachufang constitutes the largest individual source, whereas Story samples generally contain the longest interleaved sequences with around eight images per sample. At the category level, the dataset maintains relatively balanced coverage of diverse real-world content. Overall, IntReal100K contains 100K samples, 538K images, and 146.6M text tokens.

Informativeness: Does the response provide meaningful and useful content that genuinely helps the user? 2. Completeness: Does the response adequately address the full scope of the prompt without leaving key aspects unaddressed? 3. Logical coherence: The response must be smooth and sensible continuation. It should focus on the same topic/event without abrupt topic shifts or sudden logical leaps. 3. Real-world Factuality: For creative/fictional tasks (e.g., storytelling, sci-fi), allow for imaginative elements, judging only by internal consistency. For non-creative/factual tasks, the response must not severely contradict common sense or real-world logic. Important: The model response is extracted from an interleaved text-image sequence. It may contain placeholders like [image] or other special tokens. You should IGNORE these placeholders and evaluate ONLY the logical coherence and factuality of the actual text content. Output Format: You must output ONLY single valid JSON object and nothing else. No explanations, no analysis, no markdown. {coherent: true} if the model response is consistent. {coherent: false} if the model response is inconsistent. Output EXACTLY: {passes: [true, false, true, ...]} The boolean array MUST have the same length as the number of rubric items (one boolean per item, in order). sections.content: C.1 MODEL TRAINING SETTINGS We build on the official codebases of Bagel and SenseNova-U1 for SFT, with their hyperparameters summarized in Table 5. The two models use different visual representations and consequently organize their visual tokens in the KV cache differently. In Bagel, reference images in the prompt are represented by both VAE latent tokens and ViT embeddings, whereas generated images use only VAE latent tokens. SenseNova-U1 instead performs visual understanding and generation in pixel space, using representations derived from image patches. To accommodate their different visual token budgets, we adopt model-specific smart resizing strategies that preserve aspect ratios and align spatial dimensions to the required grids. For Bagel, the VAE pathway uses maximum-edge limit of 768 pixels and target minimum short edge of 512 pixels, with dimensions aligned to multiples of 16; the ViT pathway uses corresponding settings of 518, 224, and 14. For SenseNova-U1, nativeresolution resizing constrains image areas to 512210242 pixels for understanding and 768210242 pixels for generation, with dimensions aligned to the required patch grid. Detailed RL hyperparameters are provided in Table 6. We initialize Bagel and SenseNova-U1 from their SFT checkpoints at steps 4,500 and 6,900, respectively, using non-EMA weights. Given the limited SFT data and training steps, we found that EMA weights lagged behind the updated language branch, resulting in underfitting. We then perform RL post-training using Flow-Factory. C.2 MODEL INFERENCE SETTINGS During inference, models generate text autoregressively and switch to image generation when the special <image> token is produced. We follow the reasoning and generation template used by Emu3.5 (Cui et al., 2025) for interleaved generation. Unless otherwise specified, all generated images are produced at resolution of 1024 1024 for both holistic and fine-grained evaluation. We recommend 1024 1024 as the default inference resolution, as it provides sufficient visual fidelity while avoiding excessive growth in visual tokens and the resulting interleaved context length. Most models are successfully evaluated on all 600 samples in the evaluation set. However, for Emu3.5, eight samples exceed the maximum context length or memory limits even on 8H80080G GPUs, so we report its results on the remaining 592 samples. For NanoBanana2, two samples repeatedly triggered the APIs built-in safety guardrails and could not be processed, so we report its results on the remaining 598 samples. Manual inspection revealed no apparent safety concerns in these two samples, suggesting that the guardrails may have been falsely triggered.
